items.prompt: Tap every square the white knight on e5 attacks (a square holding a piece counts).

claims.statement: The knight on e5 attacks exactly these squares.

hints: A knight moves two squares one way and one the other.
Start from e5 and go two up or down, then one sideways, then two sideways, then one up or down.
Eight squares: c4, c6, d3, d7, f3, f7, g4 and g6.
items.explain: A knight on e5 reaches eight squares. Two of them matter now: g6 holds Black's bishop and f7 is the square White's pieces will aim at next. Black has to answer the attack on g6 before anything else.

items.prompt: Black to move. The bishop on g6 is attacked. Which retreat does the engine rate best?

claims.statement: 8...Bf5 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
8...Bf7 scores at least 50 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which retreat square keeps the bishop out of the knight's reach and still guards e6?
Compare f7, f5, e4 and h7: which of them can White chase with a pawn, and which can the pieces attack twice?
The bishop goes to f5.
items.explain: On f5 the bishop leaves the knight's reach and guards e6. White can chase it with g4, but the bishop then has h7. On f7 the bishop is attacked by the knight, has only the king to defend it, and must keep guarding e6. The engine (depth 16) prefers f5 by roughly six tenths of a pawn, a little more or less from run to run.

feedback_by_move.g6f7: Bf7 is the move all six players chose. The knight attacks it, only the king defends it, and the engine rates it lower than Bf5.

items.prompt: White to move. Which bishop move attacks the pawn on e6, the pawn that Black's bishop on f7 defends?

claims.statement: 9.Bc4 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
After 9.Bc4 one white piece attacks e6.
After 9.Bd3 no white piece attacks e6.
9.Bd3 scores at least 20 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which diagonal passes through e6?
A bishop on that diagonal attacks the pawn.
Bishop from f1 to c4.
items.explain: From c4 the bishop looks along c4-d5-e6 and attacks the pawn on e6, which Black's bishop on f7 defends. The knight on e5 attacks that same bishop, so the defender is under fire: if it is taken, e6 loses its guard. From d3 the bishop looks toward h7 and e6 is not attacked. The engine (depth 16) rates 9.Bd3 lower than 9.Bc4, by a few tenths of a pawn that vary from run to run.

feedback_by_move.f1d3: Bd3 does not attack e6. One game in our file used it and the higher-rated White player lost.

items.prompt: White to move. Name a developing move the engine rates well, one that keeps the knight on e5.

claims.statement: Qd3, Qe2 and O-O are each within 70 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
10.Nxf7 scores at least 30 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The knight on e5 is already well placed. What else is undeveloped?
The queen or the king can still move to better squares.
Qd3, Qe2 or castling short all keep the pressure.
items.explain: White still has the king in the centre and the queen at home. A queen move to d3 or e2, or castling, adds a piece to the attack and keeps the knight on e5 where it cramps Black. Taking on f7 gives up the knight that cramps Black for a bishop that was not doing much.

feedback_by_move.e5f7: Nxf7 trades White's best placed knight for the bishop on f7, and the engine (depth 16) rates it lower than the quiet developing moves.

items.prompt: Black to move, in check. Which king move does the engine rate far better?

claims.statement: 18...Kg8 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
18...Ke8 scores at least 400 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which king move stays off the diagonal that runs from b5 to e8?
Look at the c6 pawn: what is it blocking?
The king goes to g8.
items.explain: On e8 the king stands on the diagonal b5-e8, with only the c6 pawn in the way. If that pawn is pulled away, a queen check follows. On g8 the king keeps clear of that diagonal. The engine (depth 16) rates Ke8 about six pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.f7e8: Ke8 walks onto the diagonal where the c6 pawn is the only blocker, and the game ended quickly.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Ba5+ forces mate within four moves (engine, depth 16).

hints: The king on d8 has few safe squares: look for a check on the a5-d8 diagonal.
Which white piece can reach that diagonal with check?
The bishop from d2 to a5.
items.explain: The bishop checks along the diagonal to d8. If the rook takes it, the queen captures the knight on b8, which had only that rook as a defender, and it is mate. If the king steps away the queen keeps checking. The engine (depth 16) finds mate in four against best defence.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the knight move that attacks a piece nobody defends.

claims.statement: 12.Ng6 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
After 12.Ng6 the rook on h8 is the only loose black piece.

hints: Which black piece has no defender?
Which square lets the knight attack the rook?
The knight goes to g6.
items.explain: The knight on g6 attacks the rook on h8, and nothing defends the rook, so Black must move it. [I] The rook has only h7 to go to, where it stands in front of the g7 pawn and has little room. The engine (depth 16) rates Ng6 well ahead of the alternatives.

items.prompt: White to move. The game continued 16.Nxe6. Find the move the engine rates higher.

claims.statement: 16.Bg6+ is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
16.Nxe6 scores at least 100 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Look for a check against the king on e8.
The knight on f4 guards a square on the diagonal d3-g6.
Bishop from d3 to g6, check.
items.explain: The bishop checks the king on e8 through f7, and the knight on f4 guards g6 so the check cannot be met by a capture. Black has to block on f7 with the bishop. Then the knight takes e6, attacking the queen, and wins it for the pieces it gives. The engine (depth 16) rates this about 1.7 pawns higher than the game move.

feedback_by_move.f4e6: The game move also wins a pawn and is still good, but the check wins more.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the capture with check that mates in two.

claims.statement: 25.Qxd8+ forces mate in two (engine, depth 16).

hints: The black king has no flight squares: what is next to it?
The queen can capture with check on the back rank.
Queen f6 takes d8.
items.explain: The queen takes the rook with check along the eighth rank. The king on a8 cannot move because its own pawns block a7 and b7. The only block is the knight, ...Nc8, and the queen takes it with mate. That is a back-rank mate in two.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 10...Qc8 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
After 10...Qc8 11.Nxf7 Kxf7 12.Qf5 two black pieces defend e6.
10...Nbd7 scores at least 150 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: After a knight capture on f7 and the king recapture, how many white pieces can attack e6?
Which black piece could join the defence of e6 if it moved first?
The queen goes to c8 and guards e6 through d7.
items.explain: From c8 the queen looks through d7 at e6, so after Nxf7 Kxf7 and Qf5 the pawn is defended twice instead of once. On d7 the knight would block that diagonal and e6 would have one defender. The engine (depth 16) rates ...Nbd7 about two pawns lower than ...Qc8.

feedback_by_move.b8d7: Nbd7 blocks the d7 square and leaves e6 with one defender: Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf5 follows.

items.prompt: White to move after 10...Nbd7. Find the capture that exploits the blocked d7 square.

claims.statement: 11.Nxf7 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
The engine (depth 16) rates the position as clearly better for White (+100 to +400 cp).

hints: Which black piece is attacked twice and defended once?
The bishop on f7 has the king as its only defender. What follows if the king takes?
Knight from e5 takes on f7.
items.explain: The knight takes the bishop on f7 and the king must recapture. Then the queen goes to f5, and e6 is attacked by the queen and the bishop while only the king defends it. Black has no time to bring another defender. The engine (depth 16) rates the position clearly better for White.

items.prompt: White to move. The game continued 26.Rd1. Find the rook move that also attacks a loose piece.

claims.statement: 26.Re1 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
After 26.Re1 one white piece attacks e4.
26.Rd1 scores at least 100 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The rook on a1 is attacked and must move. Which black piece has no defender?
Which square for the rook attacks that piece along a file?
The rook from a1 to e1.
items.explain: The bishop on b2 attacks the rook, so the rook must move, and the knight on e4 has no defender. Re1 moves the rook with tempo and attacks the knight, so Black must move it or lose it. After the game move Rd1 nothing is attacked. The engine (depth 16) rates 26.Rd1 about two pawns lower.

feedback_by_move.a1d1: Rd1 saves the rook and takes the open file but attacks nothing, and the engine rates it about two pawns lower than Re1.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight on e6 attacks the queen and a bishop. What does the engine recommend?

claims.statement: 7...fxe6 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
7...Qd6 scores at least 200 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which piece attacks the knight on e6?
A pawn can capture it.
The f-pawn takes: fxe6.
items.explain: The pawn on f7 attacks e6 and takes the knight for nothing. Moving the queen away leaves the knight alive and lets it take the bishop on f8 next. Taking is the simple, best answer. The engine (depth 16) rates the queen moves about two pawns lower.

feedback_by_move.d8d6: The queen escapes but the knight takes the bishop on f8, and the engine rates the position far better for White.

items.prompt: White has just played 9.Bc4. Is the pawn on e6 attacked by a white piece?

claims.statement: One white piece attacks e6.

hints: Follow the diagonal from c4.
The only square between c4 and e6 is d5.
Yes: the bishop.
items.explain: The bishop on c4 looks along the diagonal c4-d5-e6, and d5 is empty, so it attacks the pawn on e6. That pawn is defended by the bishop on f7, which the knight on e5 attacks.

items.prompt: Same position, but White played 9.Bd3 instead. Is the pawn on e6 attacked by a white piece?

claims.statement: No white piece attacks e6.

hints: Only one thing changed: the bishop's square.
Where does a bishop on d3 look?
No: nothing attacks e6.
items.explain: From d3 the bishop looks along the diagonal d3-h7 and the other one toward a6, so e6 is not attacked and the bishop on f7 has nothing to protect.

items.prompt: Same position, but White played the quiet 9.h4. Is the pawn on e6 attacked by a white piece?

claims.statement: No white piece attacks e6.

hints: The pawn move does not touch e6.
Which white pieces see e6 now?
No: nothing attacks it.
items.explain: The rook pawn move changes nothing about e6: the knight on e5 does not attack that square and no bishop looks at it. The pawn move is irrelevant to the question.

items.prompt: Black to move after 9.Bc4. Find the developing move the engine rates best.

claims.statement: 9...Nf6 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
9...Nd7 scores at least 300 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
9...b5 scores at least 400 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which piece can develop without blocking the d7 square?
The king's knight has a good square near the centre.
The knight from g8 to f6.
items.explain: The king's knight goes to f6, where it covers e4, d5 and the d7 square for later and leaves the queen's knight free. The queen's knight move to d7 loses to Nxf7, and the pawn push b5 loses to the bishop sacrifice on e6. The engine (depth 16) rates both of these several pawns worse than Nf6.

feedback_by_move.b8d7: Nd7 blocks the queen's route and Nxf7 Kxf7 Qg4 follows.
feedback_by_move.b7b5: The pawn push attacks the bishop but Bxe6 wins at once.

items.prompt: White to move after 9...Nd7. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 10.Nxf7 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
The engine (depth 16) rates the position as clearly winning for White (at least +200 cp).

hints: Which black piece is attacked twice and defended once?
The bishop on f7 is attacked by the knight and the bishop. What takes it?
Knight e5 takes f7.
items.explain: The knight takes the bishop on f7 and the king has to recapture, because the d7 knight cannot. Then the queen reaches g4, attacking e6 a second time. The engine (depth 16) rates this as winning for White.
